title: Cooling rate and glassy behavior in the Fermi--Pasta--Ulam system
authors: Matteo Razza, Andrea Carati, Luigi Galgani
abstract: In this work, we numerically studied the cooling process of a Fermi--Pasta--Ulam system, which occurs when the FPU system is placed in contact with a gas whose temperature $T$ is reduced with a certain cooling rate $ξ$. It was found that the existence of a weak stochastic threshold has a significant impact on the cooling process, because below such a stochastic threshold the specific FPU energy is larger than its temperature, i.e., the FPU system falls out of equilibrium. The difference remains finite in the limit $T \to 0$, so that the FPU system maintains a residual amount of energy $E_0$ at vanishing temperature. Our numerical simulations reveal that this energy exhibits a power--law dependence on both the system size and the cooling rate, scaling approximately as $E_{0} \sim (ξN)^{2/3}$.
summary: The paper numerically examines how a Fermi--Pasta--Ulam lattice cools when coupled to an external bath whose temperature is lowered at a specific rate. It finds that the cooling process deviates significantly from equilibrium below a stochastic threshold, leading to a measurable residual zero-point energy ($E_0$). This residual energy exhibits a predictable power-law scaling with both system size and the applied cooling rate.
main_problem: The study investigates the non-equilibrium cooling process and associated glassy behavior of a Fermi--Pasta--Ulam (FPU) system when coupled to an external bath whose temperature is reduced at a controlled rate.
main_result: The residual zero-point energy ($E_0$) maintained by the FPU system below equilibrium scales with both system size ($N$) and cooling rate ($\xi$) according to $E_{0} \sim (\xi N)^{2/3}$.
method: Numerical simulations using the Verlet method are employed to track the time evolution of energy components during the controlled cooling process.
model_or_system: The system is an FPU lattice interacting via a Lennard-Jones potential, coupled to a gas bath. The total Hamiltonian includes both the FPU dynamics and the coupling interaction potential.
key_observables: Zero-point energy ($E_0$), specific energy ($u = E/N$), and the deviation of measured energy from expected equilibrium values.
important_parameters: Cooling rate ($\xi$), system size ($N$), and the stochastic threshold below which non-equilibrium effects dominate.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on simulating the cooling process by scaling gas particle velocities at discrete steps, assuming a weak stochastic threshold dictates the onset of glassy behavior.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of kinetic energy during cooling and show how specific energy deviates from linear expectations as temperature drops, confirming power-law dependencies for $E_0$ on $N$ and $\xi$.
paper_structure: The paper details the setup of the FPU system coupled to a bath, describes the numerical simulation procedure involving controlled cooling rates ($\xi$), presents diagnostics like zero-point energy ($E_0$), and concludes with the derived power-law scaling relationship.
why_interesting: This work explores non-equilibrium dynamics in classical many-body systems, which shares conceptual links with open quantum system thermodynamics and relaxation processes studied in AMO physics.
